niche.diet: Insects on paja_dulce, ectoparasites on rondo

chains.trait: Patagial wings fold flat; small mass yields low terminal velocity.
links: 1.6 bar air increases drag, reducing terminal velocity to ~25% of Earth norms.
High drag generates lift at low speeds, making gliding energetically cheap.
Dense air favors gliding hops over flapping flight for short distances in the meadow.

skill.effect: It folds its wings flat and drifts silently through the air to ambush nearby creatures or slip away unseen.

chains.weakness: Vulnerable during wind-up and landing; slow to regain altitude.

journal.en: A green dart that forgets to fall.

plausibility.summary: At 1.6 bar, drag scales with density so falling and gliding animals see higher deceleration and lower terminal speed (canon F4/D11/D16); a short passive glide after a hop is aerodynamically easier than on Earth. A 5 m silent drift is conservative compared with sugar gliders or Draco on Earth; it reads as extended leaping with drag assist, not sustained flapping flight, which matches meadow ambush/escape and the world's 'gliding cheap, sprinting costly' feel.
fixes: At 1.6 bar, drag scales with density so falling and gliding animals see higher deceleration and lower terminal speed (canon F4/D11/D16); a short passive glide after a hop is aerodynamically easier than on Earth. A 5 m silent drift is conservative compared with sugar gliders or Draco on Earth; it reads as extended leaping with drag assist, not sustained flapping flight, which matches meadow ambush/escape and the world's 'gliding cheap, sprinting costly' feel.

analogues.organism: Northern flying squirrel (Glaucomys sabrinus) and Draco flying lizards — patagial membranes used for short directed glides between trees, not flapping.

chains.trait: Large ear-tufts detect low-frequency movements in thick fog.
links: Dawn fog obscures vision, blinding the creature at short range.
Dense air ducts low-frequency sound along the ground over long distances.
Insect movement and prey calls produce detectable low-frequency vibrations in grass.

skill.effect: Its large ear-tufts twitch strongly to catch faint vibrations, allowing it to track and locate hidden prey moving through thick fog and tall grass.

chains.weakness: Sensitive to loud high-pitched whistles that disrupt focus.

journal.en: Ears like cups; it hears the grass breathe.

plausibility.summary: Treat tufts as grass-mimic disruption (like bittern/Caprimulgus posture) plus enlarged, low-frequency-tuned ears; add brief foot/substrate vibration sensitivity for insects at 1–3 m in fog. Keep 'deaf to high whistles' (F4: high pitches die in fog anyway).

analogues.organism: Barn owl (Tyto alba) facial ruff and asymmetric ears for prey localization; great horned owl tufts are primarily display/camouflage, not acoustic funnels.

chains.trait: Curved claws and sticky tongue extract insects from grass and fur.
links: High oxygen allows costly metabolically active tongue muscles.
Ectoparasites thrive on dense rondo herds in humid air.
Insects hide deep in grass and fur; dexterity beats brute force.

skill.effect: The creature carefully grooms its companion, using its claws and tongue to pick away hidden pests. This attentive care eases the target's discomfort and strongly strengthens their bond.

chains.weakness: Distracted by prey; stops cleaning if insects appear nearby.

journal.en: It walks on giants and takes their fleas; the giants let it.

plausibility.summary: Elevated pO₂ (D10/F5) supports metabolically expensive rapid tongue projection and fine claw manipulation. D29/D canon predict ectoparasites on dense, humid-air rondo herds; a small arthropod specialist that gleans vegetation and picks ticks/fleas/lice analogues from tolerant megagrazers is a standard mutualism when the cleaner is tiny relative to the host. Dual diet (paja_dulce insects + rondo parasites) matches meadow habitat and existing rondo ecology.
fixes: Elevated pO₂ (D10/F5) supports metabolically expensive rapid tongue projection and fine claw manipulation. Dual diet (paja_dulce insects + rondo parasites) matches meadow habitat and existing rondo ecology.

analogues.organism: Red-billed oxpecker (Buphagus erythrorynchus) on large herbivores; chameleons and anteaters for tongue/claw insect extraction.

chains.trait: Dorsal green plumage matches meadow grasses.
links: Meadow producers are green by shared ancestry from the seed.
Predation pressure from garfio selects for crypsis in the meadow.
Green is the dominant reflection of the meadow light environment.

skill.effect: Reduces detection chance when standing still against meadow backgrounds.

chains.weakness: High contrast against dark basalt or snow.

journal.en: A blade of grass that walks.

plausibility.summary: Green-dominated meadow reflectance follows seed-lineage chlorophyll producers (F24/F25), not optimality — so dorsal green against paja_dulce/velilla backgrounds is honest crypsis. Garfio as meadow mesopredator supplies directional selection for stationary camouflage during dawn/dusk scanning; ventral/leg brown countershading is standard open-habitat pattern. Albino 'glow in mist' secret is consistent with loss of melanin/UV screen, not a physics break.
fixes: Green-dominated meadow reflectance follows seed-lineage chlorophyll producers (F24/F25), not optimality — so dorsal green against paja_dulce/velilla backgrounds is honest crypsis. Garfio as meadow mesopredator supplies directional selection for stationary camouflage during dawn/dusk scanning; ventral/leg brown countershading is standard open-habitat pattern. Albino 'glow in mist' secret is consistent with loss of melanin/UV screen, not a physics break.

relations.note: (council kind 'mutualism') Zancuilla cleans ectoparasites; Rondo tolerates and protects it. Rondo herds provide a mobile substrate rich in parasites.
Garfio hunts small bipeds in the meadow; Zancuilla is a common meal.

changelog.what: removed rejected references and non-existent root facts (roots recovered from the derivation items cited in the links, else F27)

body_plan.origin: Convergent biped with membranous patagium; long tibia/fibula; avian-like torso adapted for grass scanning and gliding hops.

secrets: Rare albinos glow white in the mist.
Observed digging burrows under perlilla mounds.
Mimics the call of a rondo calf to lure adults away from predators.
moments: When the dawn fog lifts, a line of Zancuillas stands perfectly still on the backs of the sleeping Rondo, their green heads nodding in unison as the sun touches the first blade of grass.

journal.en: It leaps, hangs in the thick air, and vanishes into the grass.
The giants ignore it; it is too small to matter, and too useful.
